sites.name: Black Coral Wall
sites.depthNote: Black coral from about 25 ft; deep wall on the south side

highlights.text: Black coral at about 25 ft, unusually shallow
Macro subjects for photographers

summary.text: A south-side wall named for black coral growing unusually shallow, from around 25 ft, with one of the deeper drop-offs on that coast. The sandy reef top is full of juvenile fish and a favourite with macro photographers.

s1.quote: Black Coral Wall The site is named after the black coral that can be found around 25 ft (much shallower than typical) … one of the deepest walls on the south side of the island

s2.quote: Black Coral Wall and Pretty Bush, both macro photographers’ dreams

highlights.text: Round sand crater ringed by shallow reef
Crustaceans and octopus

s1.quote: Moon Hole - Rons Wreck The site gets its name from the large round sandy crater surrounded by shallow reef … The maximum depth in the sand is 35 ft … a large variety of crustaceans and octopus

highlights.text: Seahorses, pipefish, garden eels, southern stargazer

s1.quote: Little Bight The site has a wide sand channel that starts from the beach … reef walls that start at 15 ft and gradually get deeper until they reach 70 ft … the rare Southern Stargazer

highlights.text: Swim-through caverns with glassy sweepers
Seahorses and toadfish on the reef

summary.text: A south-side reef wall off the old airstrip with a U-shaped swim-through cave around 15 ft and a sandy floor sloping to roughly 70 ft. Glassy sweepers shelter inside, and seahorses, stingrays and eagle rays are common.

s1.quote: Airport Caves The reef wall drops to about 40 ft and then extends into a sandy floor that slopes to about 70 ft. … The cave is at 15 feet. … Sea Horses and Toad Fish

s2.quote: Airport Caves offers beautiful caverns and swim-throughs, with hundreds of glassy sweepers hiding inside.

penetration.value: Several areas can be entered and explored

highlights.text: Upright wreck with many nooks and crannies

summary.text: A deliberately sunk ship standing upright on sand near the mouth of Utila harbour, with the bridge top near 65 ft and the seabed around 100 ft. Several compartments can be explored and it is full of small marine life.

s1.quote: Halliburton … its deepest point is at a 100 ft … the top of the 3-tiered bridge is at 65 ft … several interesting areas of the wreck that can be entered and explored

s2.quote: The Halliburton Wreck is a purposely sunk cargo ship that sits upright on a sandy bottom at approximately 30 meters (100 feet). … The Halliburton Wreck has numerous nooks and crannies where divers can find hidden treasures.

sites.name: Ted's Point
sites.depthNote: Wall to about 40 ft; sailboat wreck at about 60 ft

highlights.text: Small sunken sailboat at about 60 ft
Groupers, blue tang, morays, eagle rays

s1.quote: Ted's Point The top of the reef is shallow at about 10-15 ft … A small sunken sailboat wreck can be found at about 60 ft. … Groupers, Blue Tang and Green Moray Eels

highlights.text: Flounder, seahorses, pipefish and garden eels

s1.quote: Big Rock … The top of the reef is at 10-15 ft but the sand slopes down to between 60-90 ft … Flounder, Sea Horses, Pipe Fish and Pipe Horses, Garden Eels

sites.name: Stingray Point
sites.depthNote: Sand channel slopes from 20 ft to 130 ft

highlights.text: Healthy coral including huge pillar corals
Seahorses and garden eels in the sand channel

s1.quote: Stingray Point The top of the reef ranges from as little as 5 ft to about 25 ft … sloping down all the way to 130 ft … including huge pillar corals
Crossing over the western wall and heading south leads to Ron's Wreck, a small fishing boat at about 60 ft, within a U-shaped reef wall with a gently sloping sandy bottom.

highlights.text: Barracuda, spadefish, jacks and king mackerel

summary.text: A seamount a few miles off Utila's south shore, rising to about 35 ft and falling past 130 ft. Current brings schools of barracuda, jacks and spadefish, and strong flow means it is reserved for advanced divers.

s1.quote: Black Hills The top of the sea mound is at 35 ft and it slopes down to 130 ft+ at its base. … there is often some current here … Barracuda, Atlantic Spade Fish, Horse-eyed Jacks, King Mackerel

s2.quote: Black Hills is an underwater seamount located just a few miles off the southern shore of Utila. … Due to its depth and potential for strong currents, Black Hills is best suited for advanced divers.

highlights.text: Maze-like channels with scorpionfish and lobster
Cave at 70 ft with lionfish

s1.quote: The Maze The site is named after its unique maze-like channels that start at around 15 ft and drop down to 40 ft. … Towards the west there is a cave at 70 ft where Lion Fish often hide.

highlights.text: Nurse sharks, stingrays and eagle rays
Horseshoe-shaped sand channel leading to the wall

s1.quote: Spotted Bay The edge of the reef is at about 20 ft and then drops down to about 90 ft. … a horseshoe-shaped sand channel in the shallows … Nurse Sharks, Stingrays, Spotted Eagle Rays

highlights.text: Nurse sharks, turtles, morays and eagle rays

s1.quote: Raggedy Cay … The top of the reef is at 25 ft and the wall drops down to between 80-100 ft … Nurse Sharks, Turtles, Moray Eels, Spotted Eagle Rays

highlights.text: Large barrel sponges, big grouper and turtles

s1.quote: Duppy Waters … The top of the reef is at about 20-25 ft … the wall, which drops down to more than 140 ft … Large Barrel Sponges can be found along the wall

highlights.text: Swim-through at 40 ft
Southern stingrays, snapper, grouper, morays

s1.quote: Iron Bound The top of the reef is at 10-15 ft and the wall then drops down to 50ft … an interesting swim thru at 40 ft … Southern Stingrays, Snapper, Grouper, Green Moray eels
